action: As GBHackers' report advises, inspect periodic registration traffic sent to several STUN nodes over UDP, patch or retire exposed routers and DVRs, and restrict outbound UDP from embedded devices to approved destinations.
date_note: Article gives its own publication day; CNCERT's observation window ran 9 to 20 November 2026.
exec: A botnet that hides its control traffic in ordinary STUN exchanges was reported to have reached a cumulative 5,600 infected devices, per GBHackers.
geo_basis: GBHackers says the figures cover mainland China; country-level pin.
plain: A botnet that mainly targets Linux servers and IoT devices hides its remote-control messages in normal-looking STUN traffic. GBHackers says China's CNCERT counted a cumulative 5,600 infected devices.
summary: GBHackers reports that China's CNCERT observed a new variant of the Cling botnet (tracked by Fortinet as ClingSTUN) from 9 to 20 November 2026, and that the cumulative infection count reached 5,600 devices. It mainly targets Linux servers and IoT devices and hides command-and-control traffic inside STUN exchanges. The article says the authors removed the propagation, proxy and DDoS modules.
title: CNCERT reportedly sees Cling botnet variant reach 5,600 infected devices, hiding C2 in STUN traffic

validation.note: Single publisher (GBHackers) relaying CNCERT and NSFOCUS; neither original was read.

evidence.quote: the cumulative infection count reached 5,600 devices.

review.note: Compared 5,600 figure, dates, modules, platforms, advice against GBHackers
